utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Can we have the appearances?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I'm Eric Ostberg and with me appearing for the Prosecution this morning is Ms. Teresa McHenry, Mr Giuliano Turone, Mr Stefan Waespi and our case manager, Ms. Elles van Dusschoten. Thank you. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Good morning, your Honours. My name is Edina Residovic, defence counsel for Mr Zejnil Delalic. With me defending Mr Delalic is Mr Eugene O'Sullivan, Professor from Canada. MR. OLUJIC (in interpretation): Good morning, your Honours. My name is Zeljko Olujic, defence counsel for Mr Zdravko Mucic. With me in the defence team is my learned colleague, Michael Greaves, attorney from London. MR. KARABDIC (in interpretation): Good morning, your Honour. I am Salih Karabdic, lawyer from Sarajevo, defence counsel for Mr Hazim Delic. With me in the team is Mr Thomas Moran, attorney from Houston, Texas.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours. I am John Ackerman, appearing on behalf of Mr Esad Landzo. Finally she has returned to our midst. Cynthia McMurrey is back from the United States and with us today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Welcome, Cynthia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms Residovic is continuing on cross-examination. Is starting this morning reducing the time or increasing it? Have you invited the witness? (Witness enters court) (Interpreter enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly inform the witness he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr Gschwendt, may I remind you that you are still under oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (In interpretation): Yes, I understand that. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Good morning, your Honours. Good morning, Mr Gschwendt. I thought things over, your Honours, and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I have no translation.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr Gschwendt. Your Honours, I will shorten my cross-examination so as to give my colleagues a chance and to leave a couple of questions for the next witness. Thank you. Mr Gschwendt, yesterday in the course of your testimony before the court you said that you met with representatives of the International Tribunal at the hotel late at night; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion you discussed the operation that had been planned for the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The operation hadn't been scheduled for the following day. It had been scheduled for the day after that originally. The operation was planned for 19th March.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr Gschwendt, did you agree on that occasion to carry out the search and seizure of the apartment in accordance with Austrian law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, yes. In Austria we can only operate on the basis of Austrian law.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr Gschwendt, can you tell me whether it is true that during the search and confiscation of objects on the spot in the apartment in which Mr Delalic resided and in the premises of INDA-BAU, where Mr Delalic also stayed occasionally, representatives of the International Tribunal were not present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know they were not present, no.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr Gschwendt. Mr Gschwendt, can you tell me whether the right to counsel is acquired by the accused the very moment he is informed of that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a legal question that I would not feel entitled to address. A judge would be in a position to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr Gschwendt, I have followed closely your replies in answer to questions put by my distinguished colleague, Mr Moran. As you have considerable experience, is it true that in the process of the investigations carried out by the police defence counsel is not present, the defence counsel of the suspects?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this specific instance none was present, because Mr Mucic had not asked for one.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr Gschwendt, please, does the investigating judge in your country give the same warning that you give to the suspect in connection with his right to remain silent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't answer that with regard to what happens at the examining magistrate's. There's no one from the police present there. As I said yesterday, towards 1.30 in the morning, early in the morning of the 19th, in other words, Mr Mucic was transferred to the court's custody and that was the end of all contact with Mr Mucic on the part of the Vienna police.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr Gschwendt, I appreciate the fact that you are not familiar with certain legal issues, so I will not insist on those questions. However, you confirmed that you were familiar with the law on criminal procedure of Austria. Can you tell me whether according to the criminal procedure of Austria there are certain criminal offences in which defence counsel is obligatory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right. As of a certain sentence that's provided for, there are cases where the accused must have legal counsel, but that is only in respect of procedure. It has nothing to do with police measures. That is to say that is to do with the legal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, Mr Gschwendt, is defence obligatory in the case of serious criminal offences?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again that's a question that I can't answer. It's a legal issue. I'm not an expert in Austrian law, I'm afraid. I'm a policeman, an operative.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr Gschwendt, but you are familiar with the law on criminal procedure on Austria. I showed you the book yesterday and you said you were familiar with it. Isn't that so? Still I do not insist on an answer to that question, as you said you didn't know. However, as you do know that counsel is obligatory for some criminal offences, can in such a situation the accused waive his right to defence counsel according to Austrian law? Is it correct that in that case he cannot waive that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, this is in connection with legal proceedings, that is to say before the court. It's not relevant to police operation, but quite frankly I can't address these legal issues. I'm not entitled to.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr Gschwendt, the statements that you take at the police without the presence of defence counsel cannot be used as evidence in court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. Everything can be used as evidence before the court.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr Gschwendt, is it true that Vienna is a very open city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, if you're asking me for my opinion, I'd tend to say yes, but I assume there's different opinions on the subject.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a policeman you know that there are more than 100,000 foreigners living in Vienna today. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Among those more than 100,000 foreigners there are tens of thousands from the territory of the former Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, Mr Gschwendt, which peoples from the territory of the former Yugoslavia are the most represented: the Bosnians, the Serbs or the Croats? Do you have those figures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I certainly don't have the figures in my mind, but a lot of people from the former Yugoslavia fled, given the events that took place there, and I believe at one point in time it was the Bosnians that were the largest group represented, but I do not know. That's just an assumption.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the situation was before the war, which group was the most numerous?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr Gschwendt. Thank you, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr Ackerman, any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We have no questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, just a very few questions for Mr Gschwendt.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr Gschwendt, I would like to ask you if in Austrian law is there any provision which is similar to a specific Rule of this Tribunal, and I'm going to read a small part of this Rule. It says that -- Rule 10 1 says that: "In determining the sentence, the Trial Chamber shall take into account of course the statute as well as such factors as, first, aggravating circumstances, second", and this is the point, "any mitigating circumstances, including the substantial cooperation with the Prosecutor by the convicted person before or after conviction". I want to know is there any similar provision in Austrian law as to considering mitigating circumstances like that in determining the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are such legal provisions in the criminal code. There's the grounds for aggravation, the aggravating circumstances, as it were, and then the grounds for mitigation as well that are indicated, and the court applies those in sentencing.

utterances.speaker: MR TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like Mr Gschwendt to be provided with the original, for his convenience, of this arrest warrant in German concerning Zdravko Mucic in order to have some -- could you please provide him? It is one of the attachments to the bunch of papers that Mr Moran gave yesterday to the witness. The attachment in the bunch of papers was only in English and now I will provide the witness with the original in German for his convenience actually. (Handed to witness). So, would you please, Mr Gschwendt, tell the court what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document is a warrant of arrest and it was issued by judge Dr Peter Seda on 14th March 1996 and this warrant indicates that Zdravko Mucic is to be arrested so that he might be extradited to the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Republic of Yugoslavia, and there's also an indication of a suspicion concerning Mr Mucic based on him being the Commander of the Celebici prisoner camp from May 1992-November 1992 to have killed members of the Serbian ethnic group or to have contributed to their being killed, and it says "based on investigations by the Serb judicial authorities and the investigatory organs of the United Nations".

utterances.speaker: MR TURONE
utterances.text: Do you see signatures appearing at the bottom of this? Can you say which appears at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first signature there is by the judge, the investigating magistrate, and the second one, that's at the very bottom, on 18th March 1996 and the date is there, this warrant of arrest was signed by Zdravko Mucic, and the date was added.

utterances.speaker: MR TURONE
utterances.text: Mr Gschwendt, was a copy of this warrant of arrest provided to Mr Mucic and translated to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Not translated).

utterances.speaker: MR TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it would be proper to enter into evidence both this German original document and also the information sheet which was shown yesterday to the witness, both in German language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mr Turone, I just want to find out. The custody record was to be --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The last answer by the witness was "yes".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Does it say, the custody record, he should be handed over to the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina or to the Tribunal? I am just confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This is something which probably comes out with the next witness in a more clear way, but if you want me to ask this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If it comes out of the mouth of the next witness, that is sufficient for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Anyway we can say -- Mr Gschwendt, do you mean there was a request for extradition of Mr Mucic coming not only from this Tribunal but also from Bosnia-Herzegovina, I mean from the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That's not the question I asked you. I just wanted a little clarification, because the wording of the warrant as you read shows that the custody is to be handed over to the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I thought it was to be handed over to the Tribunal. It's not a question to be addressed to the witness. I'm just talking about the wording of the warrant prepared by Dr Seda, not by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. So with the tendering of these two German language originals, the information sheet and the warrant of arrest, my re-examination is finished, your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I rise, I guess, with a comment. I couldn't help but notice that during Ms Residovic's cross-examination of this witness this morning his answers were almost uniformly: "I'm not an expert on Austrian law. You'll have to ask a judge or a lawyer about that", which differs markedly from the answers he was giving yesterday. Then the very next thing that happened was when Mr Turone got up and asked him a question about Austrian law regarding the punishment under Austrian law, he all of a sudden was an expert on it again and gave a very detailed answer about what Austrian law is in that regard. If he is going to deny knowledge when we are doing cross but have that knowledge when the Prosecution is doing direct, there's something that strikes me as unfair about that. It would seem to me that perhaps, and I do not speak for Miss Residovic, perhaps either the answer he gave to Mr Turone should be struck on that basis or that Ms Residovic should be permitted to ask her questions again, now that he has decided that he does know about Austrian law.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I respond to this, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Actually we could -- all of us could appreciate that Mr Gschwendt gave in cross-examination a number, a large number of answers also on legal questions. Only in a number of extremely particular questions he replied: "I'm no lawyer, so on this field I don't feel to be in a position to give a real answer", but a number of legal questions, a number of questions on Austrian law were answered by Mr Gschwendt in the scope of his knowledge of Austrian law, because Mr Gschwendt did not deny at all to know, to have anyway a legal background of penal and criminal procedural law of his country. Simply he said that, not being a lawyer, he's not in a position to answer to questions which are too specific and too connected to the professionalism of a real lawyer. The question about the existence of mitigating and aggravating circumstances in substantial criminal law is something which absolutely is encompassed in the general knowledge of any policeman in any country of the world, and particularly the knowledge of mitigating circumstances and the knowledge of mitigating circumstances which -- the origin of which might be more or less important cooperation of the suspect and so on. So I would say the mitigating circumstances in substantial criminal law of a country are well-known to every policeman of that country. On the other hand, a question concerning legal technicalities might not be encompassed in the knowledge of police officers. This is what I feel in the duty to clarify. I think it was a matter of logic and experience of everyone sitting in this courtroom. Thank you, your Honour. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, with every respect for Mr Turone, I did not understand that Mr Turone had the function of a witness or the counsel of the witness who spoke at length here in this courtroom. I thank the witness for answering many questions showing considerable legal knowledge of the criminal procedure of Austria. I'm only concerned that this morning Mr Gschwendt suddenly forgot his legal knowledge and I fear that this may be linked to the widespread objections rejected by court yesterday, the objections of Mr Turone. However, I do indeed hope that the witness spoke the truth both yesterday and today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, on a little bit different thing, on those exhibits, I don't have any objection to their admission, so long as they are accompanied with translations into one of the two official languages of the Tribunal, preferably for me English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I explain that the translations into English are already attached to the bunch of papers Mr Moran provided yesterday the witness with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: But, your Honour, they're not evidence. They're just part of the papers of the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May I refer to --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We agree we will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Will you please sit down and let me make a point?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I refer to Mr Ackerman's observation. It is a little difficult for the Trial Chamber to determine at what point someone is telling the truth or pretending not to know or has forgotten what he knew when, in fact, he could know. That's a thing you take as a whole, not only in respect of what I think. So it is difficult in respect of that. Now I did not bother to stop Mr Turone when he put the question on re-examination, because it was obviously not relevant to the cross-examination, which merely pointed out the effect on questioning, on what was told the accused person on questioning. Now, the knowledge which was brought was something on mitigation of sentence, sentencing procedure, which is quite different. I just ignored it, because I knew it had nothing to do with the cross-examination. So sometimes you might ignore these things when, in fact, it makes no difference to your case whichever way one took it. Now, Mr Gschwendt has given purely factual evidence and where he's unable as a police officer to come to conclusions on law, he stated that, and I wouldn't for that regard his testimony on those areas where he said he couldn't give legal opinion as suspect. It's possible he couldn't, or even if he knew, he wouldn't. Well, it might be an aspect of non-cooperation, but I don't think that's a reason why one should impose any sanctions for that. Thank you very much for your observation. Thank you very much, Mr Gschwendt. I think you are finished. I think that's all we have for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. (Witness withdrew) (Interpreter withdrew).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I was just wondering: this lady is not going to help the next witness in German.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, the next witness is German, too. The next witness for the Prosecution is Mr Thomas Moerbauer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: We are trying to find out whether the arrangement for assistance is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I guess so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Call her back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Please swear the witness. Mr. Thomas Moerbauer (sworn)

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I proceed, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Sir, can you please state your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Thomas Moerbauer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Which is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 29th August 1966.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Which is your citizenship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm an Austrian citizen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What is your profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you say exactly which position you have inside the Austrian police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a District Inspector and I work, as said, in the Austrian police in that capacity.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you say in which unit of the Austrian --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Hold on. Is the witness not interested in interpretation. He has not put on his headphones.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the interpreter might just briefly explain that the witness does not understand English and therefore the interpreter is translating into German for Mr. Moerbauer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He doesn't have to put them on if he doesn't understand English. He doesn't understand any other languages here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, can you say in which unit of the Austrian police you work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Division 1 in the Vienna Police Department. That's for State protection. It's protection of State matters and individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you have the same position in March 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I had that same position.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In which year did you get such position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1992, October.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you please describe briefly your professional curriculum starting from the type of school you attended before entering police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I went to basic school until I was 15. In 1981, September, I started with the police school in Vienna as a police cadet. In 1984 I was a fully-fledged police officer and I served for four years in Vienna. Then I was with the police in Schiket (sic). Then in 1991/1992, I took a detective course. In October of 1992 I joined Division 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In which year did you become District Inspector?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Moerbauer, coming back to your present position, where are located the premises of the 1st Division where you currently work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the 1st District Schottenring 7-9 is the address.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Is that in the centre of Vienna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is in the centre of Vienna.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Is that the central headquarters of the Austrian Federal Police in Vienna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It's the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In your official capacity of police officer of the First Division do you usually carry on criminal investigations on particular crimes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Which kind of crimes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Crimes having to do with State security, normally threats to neutrality, so they're quite specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Before this present occasion did you have other occasions to testify in court as a result of your investigative work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Moerbauer, are you aware of a request of cooperation signed by the Prosecutor of this Tribunal and directed to the Austrian authorities for the arrest of Mr. Zdravko Mucic and Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did that request also concern the fulfillment of searches and seizures of material related to the same proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you personally take part to the police operations concerning all this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did these police operations take place in cooperation with Interpol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now I know you have your notes with you, so I might ask the Trial Chamber to allow the witness to consult his notes and files from now on in order to refresh your memory. So, Mr. Moerbauer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute. These notes were prepared contemporaneously or later?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Exactly as the other witness, being a police officer, I think he might be allowed to consult his own notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I'm asking when were these notes prepared from which he wants to refresh his memory?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Where did you prepare your notes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: When did you prepare your notes, Mr. Moerbauer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The notes are basically copies of the reports and there's three pages that I have a written up to set out the case chronologically. About two or three weeks ago I did that, set it out chronologically on the basis of the police file.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, Mr. Moerbauer, was there a time when you met with some Interpol officers in order to prepare the police operations we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was on 12th March 1996. Magistrate Gross and Administrative Officer Furst from Interpol came into our office and that's when we had that discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: When were you informed in some detail about the charges raised by the Prosecution of this Tribunal against Mr. Delalic and Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first information came to me on 6th March through my colleague Panzer, and I happened to be on holiday. He gave me a phone call and said there had been this request relating to Zdravko Mucic, and he knew that that name was one I was familiar with, that I might know something more about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, was there any extradition request coming from a given State concerning Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were requests from Yugoslavia to the Federal Ministry of Justice and via the Department 210 that was passed on to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: When did the request of Yugoslavia arrive to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The request came in to us on 6th March, into the Police Department in Vienna, that is to say my department.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: When did the request coming from the Prosecutor of this Tribunal come to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A bit later. Let me have a look here at my documents. On 13th March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So I think we had some misunderstanding in your previous answer. I ask again: when were you informed in some details of the charges raised by the Prosecutor of this Tribunal against Mr. Delalic and Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 13th March 1996 from the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you have an occasion to talk with people of Interpol about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On 12th March when discussing Mucic I mentioned that Mucic worked at a company that belonged apparently to the Delalic family and somebody from Interpol said that there were investigations going on about Delalic, but that was in Germany, and that was on account of a request from the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Before this which is happening on March 1996, were the names of Mr. Delalic and Mr. Mucic already known to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you explain for which reasons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1992 from a refugee camp in Vienna there were some passports that were stolen, and we found them in a cafe which belonged to Sefic Delalic, who in the meantime had passed away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Please speak slower when you give these accounts but there is some --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this evidence on the grounds that it is (a) neither relevant, and (b) its prejudicial effect frankly outweighs any relevance it may have. I suspect that the evidence that my learned friend is seeking to adduce is going to be evidence concerning investigations by police officers. It is a general principle of law that evidence concerning any previous wrong doing by any person is not admissible as evidence, and it is usually treated as evidence which is wholly prejudicial. In my respectful submission, this is just such evidence, and I would respectfully invite your Honours not to permit these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I think the relevancy -- the possibility that the two suspects were already known to this witness might be anyway relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You can re-word the question. He came to know the names in the course of investigation in another case, not about what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Not the details of what happened. You don't start with wrongdoing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The details of the previous investigation are not relevant. So, coming back to this case and the case concerning this Tribunal, when did the Austrian judge issue the arrest warrants and the search warrants concerning Delalic and Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The warrant of arrest was from 14th March. That's when we received them from Department 210. They passed them on to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did that concern both arrest warrant and search warrants, the 14th March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two arrest warrants and four search warrants.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you know from where did Judge Seda receive the relevant information prior to issuing the arrest and search warrants?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, he can't answer questions about what someone else knew and where someone else got information from.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Well, the source for the judge might have been in whole or in part the witness himself, or he might know for official reasons how much the judge received the relevant informations. So may I proceed to this question, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Ask him did he supply the information to the judge. Why go round about that way? Did he place the papers before the judge? Ask him straight.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you directly give Judge Seda the relevant information prior to issuing the arrest and search warrants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That is not how it's commonly done. It always goes through the legal department or by some other department. So it doesn't go through the Police Department proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Moerbauer, how many places were supposed to be searched according to the warrants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four localities were to be searched. In fact, there were five locations because there was Koppstrasse 14 and Koppstrasse 16 that were referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In particular can you say which places were supposed to be searched?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The company offices primarily, which were connected with the two individuals, that is to say Mucic and Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes. Can you please go into more details and say exactly all the addresses and the premises where searches were supposed to take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, according to the first search warrant it was in the 17th District, Taubergasse 15, the club premises, the BiH club rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Speak slowly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So 17th district, Taubergasse 15. The BiH club facilities, and in that building there's also the apartment of Delalic and the company premises of the MAS company, that is to say they have their offices there. Now the second address was Vienna 16, Koppstrasse 14. That is where the MAS company had its official headquarters. Third search was to be in 1160 Vienna, Koppstrasse 14 and 16. That was the headquarters of the INDA-BAU company. In 1160 Hasnerstrasse 32, that is the official headquarters of the Rimebau company. In Hasnerstrasse 32, there is also the apartment of the brother, Djemal Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, how was the INDA-BAU firm related to either Mucic or Delalic or both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The INDA-BAU company was run by relatives of Zejnil Delalic. Mucic worked at INDA-BAU as a bricklayer but this was some time ago. His last employer was the MAS company.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you give us some specific information on the ownership, controller directorship of this INDA-BAU firm?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I have to object, your Honours, as to relevancy of these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The relevancy is due to the fact that we have a search having taken place in the premises of INDA-BAU firm and seizure of documents having taken place in the INDA-BAU firm, and the connection between Delalic and the INDA-BAU firm is relevant, and so any question about the directorship and so on of the firm might be relevant. May the witness be allowed to answer this question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The companies in question had been checked previously and the connections were ascertained with Mucic and Delalic. These findings on 12th March were -- that information was passed on to the people from Department 210 and they were provided with copies from our file and those documents were passed on to Dr Seda by Department 210 and on the basis of that information Dr Seda issued the search warrants, but those addresses weren't 100 per cent up-to-date, and that's -- for instance, the INDA-BAU headquarters was in Koppstrasse 14 on the ground floor, and with respect to INDA-BAU, there was a sign, a note, a sign there saying that Koppstrasse 14 was also where the MAS company was headquartered. At that time Mucic was also the manager of the MAS company, or shall we say he was employed with the MAS company, and all of the addresses were given a serious look and it was decided there should be a change made, and there again the information was passed on via Department 210 to Dr Seda, so that the search warrants could be corrected. The following addresses were then suggested. This is in the 17th District, Taubergasse 15, Door 10, and that is the apartment of Mucic. Taubergasse 15, Door 14, that's the former apartment of Zejnil Delalic. He'd lived there until November 1995. That's where he was living, and Taubergasse 15 there, that building was one that was leased to MAS, and MAS was also the landlord, the provider of housing, as it were, for the various apartments and that could be determined on the basis of the registration information. Now a further search warrant was requested for Taubergasse 28. That was where the MAS company had its workshops. In the apartment of Djemal Delalic, in the 16th district, Hasnerstrasse 32, Door 27-29, and it could be assumed that Zejnil Delalic may well be found there. In other words, there wasn't any official registration on the part of Zejnil Delalic in Vienna, official registration as living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. Can you have some specific information on the directorship, ownership, control of the MAS firm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as to who was controlling the companies, now that information led us to believe that Zejnil Delalic was the one who was really running things. Now officially friends and relatives of Zejnil Delalic were running the companies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we can break here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This information is hearsay. What is the source of this information?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What is the source of this information, Mr. Moerbauer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Investigations went on for a year concerning these companies, and the club, for instance, was also contacted, and Djemal Delalic was also doing business operations in Vienna, and Zenjil Delalic on the basis of information from informers and other people who had contacts with his companies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Then you have to produce witnesses who are direct to his knowledge. He is merely drawing inferences from hearsay evidence. How is that relevant or of great value?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think let's break here. We'll come back at 11.30. (11.10 am) (Short break) (11.35am) (Witness re-entered court) (Interpreter re-entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly remind him he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: You are --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I proceed, your Honour? I got a translation into French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO BENITO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We need some English translation on channel 4. Is the English translation now?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear me? This is the English channel.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Moerbauer. Were the two apartments of Delalic and Mucic in the same building in Taubergasse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Are Koppstrasse, where the INDA-BAU was located, and Taubergasse close to each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 300-500 metres apart as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Are they located in the centre of Vienna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It's in outer district, beyond the Belt as it's called. The Belt goes round the inner area, and it's beyond the Belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: When and where was Mr. Mucic arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mucic was arrested on 18th March, 2.15 in the afternoon, in the street Nattagasse. That's the street that's parallel to Taubergasse.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: As far as you know, when and where was Mr. Delalic arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know he was arrested at roughly the same time in Munich.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you please tell the court what happened and what did you do between March 14th and March 18th as far as the police observations which led to this joint arrest operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 14th March an observation unit started watching Taubergasse 15. We took it that Mucic would be appearing there and that Delalic might be appearing there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Speak slowly, please, Mr. Moerbauer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And in the evening hours Panzer and myself went to Mucic's apartment and said that we were looking for someone -- well, not a person -- we were carrying out a registration. We came up with the name of Manminic (sic), but said that was just a pretence, because we wanted to see whether Mucic was actually on the premises. In the apartment we chanced upon Mucic and his daughter and that way we could ascertain that Mucic was actually residing at his official place of residence. We did not encounter Delalic in the apartment on that occasion. Then as from 16th March the observations were carried out on a more reinforced basis, because should Mucic and Delalic appear together our plans were to arrest them together on that occasion. Then on 16th March, 7 o'clock in the morning at Taubergasse 30 there was a vehicle with Munich plates that was spotted there, and we checked out the vehicle and we found that it had been registered with the Insunt company. So we thought that maybe Zejnil Delalic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: The witness appears to be reeding from some kind of a script. If he is using his notes, that is one thing, but if he is reading from a script we would ask that it be translated into English. It might save us all some trouble?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fine. 7 o'clock we spotted this vehicle and there was a suspicion that this was the vehicle of Zejnil Delalic. Now in the course of the afternoon at 2.15 in the afternoon Delalic left the house through the entrance at Taubergasse 15 and he came through the exit of the club rooms, went to the vehicle with the German licence plates and drove to Koppstrasse, Kopp Street. There he went into the premises of the INDA-BAU company, came back into the street accompanied with a 30 year old woman approximately with dark hair and put files into his vehicle. So he was in the company premises for about half an hour or so, and then alone he drove towards the border crossing at Walzberg and he left Austria at about 6 o'clock that afternoon. Now, we did not proceed to an arrest. We had agreed with the German colleagues that we would only take action if we were sure that both individuals -- shall we say, rather, if we chanced upon both individuals together, which was not the case. Now Mucic, shortly after Delalic left, started going to Koppstrasse. Mucic at all events came out of the apartment, drove off, but then we lost track of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I have to slow you down again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So as regards the observation of Mucic, that could not be pursued. So that's why we decided we would not arrest Delalic, and the German authorities were notified and, as we had agreed, the German authorities would be taking over observation then in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: When you went and met Mr. Mucic in his apartment on March 14th, in what language did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We spoke in German.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did he answer in German?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Again concerning the observation you personally did between March 14th and March 18th, was there a time when you had a chance to observe again Mr. Mucic in any situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Mucic was observed -- well, in between -- I don't know just when that was, whether it was on 16th or 17th. He was driving a vehicle of the INDA company. It was registered with INDA-BAU. He drove to the belt. He was spotted there and on 18th in the course of the morning he was preparing a vehicle, not the INDA-BAU vehicle but a different vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, did you personally take part in the arrest of Mr. Mucic on March 18th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you give us the names of your colleagues who joined you in this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were officers Panzer, Borlak and Bycek.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Who for you was the head of the patrol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Panzer was in charge of the patrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you tell the court how did the arrest take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mucic was observed while he was preparing this vehicle. It looked like a good time to take action, because Mucic was there on his own. Now, we talked to Gschwendt at the office to say this would be a good time to go ahead. We got the go ahead and myself and Panzer came out of our vehicle, went up to Mucic at his vehicle and arrested him. We passed on the information that he was arrested. He had his hands handcuffed behind his back and after that we went to Mucic's apartment, and when Mucic was arrested, he was told why he was arrested, that it was on the basis of a court arrest warrant, as there was a suspicion of crimes in the Celebici camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Was there any ICTY investigator present at the arrest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you immediately inform Mr. Gschwendt about the arrest of Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not report to him, but immediately after the arrest he was informed of the arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What happened right after the arrest of Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went into the apartment, Taubergasse 15, Door 10, together with Mucic and his daughter was in the apartment. We opened the handcuffs from behind Mucic's back and closed them again with his hands in front again. We sat down at the table. Mucic was sitting there. Panzer sat there. Once again he was informed as to the grounds of the arrest, what was going on, and he was informed that there would be searches on the premises, that there were search warrants and then the search began.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: At what time did the search in Mucic's apartment start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At about fifteen minutes after the arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Was this search done by you together with the same three colleagues who were with you at the arrest of Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you give Mucic a copy of the arrest warrant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you have the arrest warrant read to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What kind of an information you gave to Mr. Mucic about his arrest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That he was allegedly camp commander in Celebici. Crimes had been committed there, and in that connection the Vienna District Criminal Court had issued an arrest warrant. It was Dr Seda who had issued the warrant.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you give Mucic a copy of the search warrant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't give him a copy, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Was the search warrant explained to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The search warrant was explained to him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In which language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In German and Sanda Mucic, his daughter, also translated it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did Sanda Mucic speak fluent German?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you give any further information or explanation to Mr. Mucic in this very moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We said that there was a possibility that he might be handed over to The Hague and he was also given the possibility that after the search he could take along some luggage, as it were, some personal items, because he may be in custody for some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: How long did the search in Mucic's apartment last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you seize any material?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I seized the videotapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: But was there any other material seized in Mucic's apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the apartment there were several diaries, I believe, that were seized. Then various identification papers. There were Yugoslavian passports there, identity cards. There were handcuffs there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: How many videotapes did you seize there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four videotapes in Mucic's apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In which room exactly did you seize these four videotapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The videotapes were in the living room and they were in a cabinet, and there were other videotapes there, but they were commercial videotapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Well, at the end of the search where did you put the seized material? I mean, some bags, some box?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We put them in plastic bags or boxes. I don't remember quite what they were. I think there were both plastic bags and boxes used.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you prepare a search record, a Niederschrift, for this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We began with the record, the Niederschrift, in Mucic's apartment, but the seized objects, as regards them, they were indicated later on in the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Mucic sign this search record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you remember when did he sign this search record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When? No, I don't remember, but it must have been in the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You mean in police headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you mean the same day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the same day, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Was the record read out to Mr. Mucic by an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did that occur later on in the police headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The interpreter was in the office, shall we say, at the police headquarters as of 4 o'clock and began with the formalities that are required subsequent to an arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. We'll come to that later. On which floor was -- on which floor in the building of Taubergasse was the apartment of Mucic located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mucic's apartment, the first floor, that is to say one flight up. There's sort of a mezzanine, but it is basically the first floor, one flight up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What about the apartment of Delalic? Was that on the same floor of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's one flight of stairs up in the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you personally take part in the search of Delalic's apartment as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not involved in the search, because -- well, rather, a colleague came down into Mucic's apartment and he told me that there were a lot of documents that had been seized in that apartment, and I went to, quote, Delalic's apartment upstairs, and there was a bag on the desk and the videotapes were already in there and there was a pile of documents, and the colleague said these were matters relating to Yugoslavia. I said: "Yes, we'll take those along as well." Then I went back down to Mucic's apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you give us the names of your colleagues who carried on the search in Delalic's apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unger and Winkelmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did they have the keys of Delalic's apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as to how they got the keys, I can't say. I came later. I went back up to the apartment, and when we locked the door, they gave me the keys, the seized objects and the record, and Harija (sic) Delalic, that is to say the sister-in-law of Zejnil Delalic, was to receive the keys; that is, I was to give them to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You said Harija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Harija.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Where does this person live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was in the apartment that was next to Mucic's apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you say approximately when did the search start in the apartment of Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The searches all took place roughly at the same time. There could have been a difference of some ten, fifteen minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Who was present as a witness on Delalic's behalf during the search in that apartment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But he was not present when the search took place. He was not present is what he said. He came later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Then I'll reword my answer (sic). Did Sanda Mucic stay always in Mucic's apartment during the time you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when I was upstairs briefly, I only saw Harija Delalic the first time I saw the objects. When the apartment was locked Sanda Mucic was no longer there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: During this time when you went back and forth from the apartment of Delalic to the apartment of Mucic, did you personally see whether a search record was immediately done concerning the search in Delalic's apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. When it was locked, the seized objects and the record, along with the keys, were handed to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: By whom was that record signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I could make out, on the record there was the two officers who had signed and Sanda Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did the colleagues who carried on the search in Delalic's apartment join you after the search?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Where did they join you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the police headquarters, in our offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Was the whole seized material carried there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The seized material was brought there and the two colleagues had gone ahead, because there is a report. After a search you have to draw up a report about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you personally see again in the police premises the same days the material which was seized in Delalic's apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did see it, and I took it along to headquarters as well. I took it to the colleagues who wrote the report, because I was waiting for their report of the search.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Was there any file containing paper documents among the materials seized in Delalic's apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: How many folders? How many files?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember in Delalic's apartment there was only one file.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Where was all this material, I mean the Delalic's apartment material, put? I mean, into bags or boxes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He has already said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: That was about the other search.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He was talking about Delalic's apartment. He said when he went to the room of Delalic they were in a plastic bag or a box?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was Mucic, Mucic's apartment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I misunderstood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a large black sports bag and that's what the objects were in, and we also took that sports bag and we gave it as identification number D1.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you say at what time was the search concluded in Delalic's apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was one of the last ones we finished with in that building. Just exactly when, it must have been about 4.00 pm, at about 4.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Was any other search fulfilled in that same building of Taubergasse 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Taubergasse 15 there was another search there in the club premises, this is the BiH club. I was present, Bycek and another officer was there as well. You could find out who it was precisely in the records but no objects were seized there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What happened when all the searches inside that building were concluded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we went to police headquarters, Schottenring, with Mucic, and we went up to the third floor, to Room 331. Now, the interpreter was already present in that room and we began filling out the various sheets, personal data, custody report. There are a number of forms that have to be filled out and I was busy gathering the reports about the searches, because the colleagues were in various rooms, so we have various copies that have to be made, and I only filled out the personal data part of the required report, shall we say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Approximately at what time did you arrive at the central police headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between 4.30 and 5 o'clock in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You said you went to Room 331. Was the seized material brought to that same room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was brought to that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What was Room 331 normally used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those are our offices. Panzer, Bycek and myself have our offices there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Who was inside Room 331 when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The interpreter was there and first Lieutenant Gschwendt. That was his rank at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you repeat the name of the interpreter. I do not remember if you said that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Liliana Supput is the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Right after arriving there did you say anything to Mr. Mucic at this point with the help of the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You were talking about the formalities and documents. Was there documents concerning personally Mucic which were dealt with right after arriving to the ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now I'm not sure I understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I mean, my question is: right after arriving at the police headquarters with Mucic, right after arrival in that room where Gschwendt and the interpreter was, was something explained to Mucic with the help of the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In connection with the formalities and the custody record there's also the information sheet for arrested persons there, and I didn't start filling out that custody report with Mucic. Somebody else did that. But there's also the various items in there, the notification of consular representation, consultation of a lawyer, but I did not go through that myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So somebody else did inform Mucic about his rights?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I got the custody report later. I was not there when that was translated to him; at least, I wasn't paying any attention to it and can't say anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you see whether Mr. Mucic signed any document right after his arrival at the police headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Mucic remain in Room 331 after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We took him up there, the colleagues who carried out the arrest. Whether all four were there I can't really say, but I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: How long did Mr. Mucic remain in Room 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, while I was there, he was there the whole time. He may have been out for a moment here or there. He was in the arrest cell for discussion. I can't say whether he was in there the whole time until the relevant document was drawn up, but most of the time I would say he was in the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did he ever remain alone in Room 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was never alone in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, who are the colleagues of yours who carried on the search of the premises in the INDA-BAU?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Navarat, an officer in the division, and then there were two officers from the 16th District police station, Knauder and Klauser are the officers from that district.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did any of these police officers also come to Room 331 in that same afternoon of March 18th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the same afternoon First Lieutenant Navrat came into the room and gave me the seized objects.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Approximately at what time did he come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the last officer to give me material, so it must have been after 3 o'clock -- sorry -- rather after 5 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Can you say approximately through the records you received and saw at what time did the search start in the INDA-BAU premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The searches were to start at roughly the same time. There were some delays, 15, 20 minutes, because the arrest came about unexpectedly, rather it happened earlier than planned, so that led to some delays. Then as regards the search of Koppstrasse I can't say exactly when that began, but that should be in the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: By the way, was any material seized in the INDA-BAU premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, material was seized at INDA-BAU.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: As far as you know, who was present as a witness on behalf of the suspect during the search in the INDA-BAU premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, Elvir Rizvanovic was present and a woman whose last name was Delalic -- Suana or something. I'm not sure. The other person was Elvir Rizvanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you say at what time a search record was done concerning the search in the INDA-BAU premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The record as a rule is filled out on the spot. The only exception was in connection with Mucic. There we filled that out in the office in police headquarters. The protocol, the record that has to be filled out on the spot, because a copy is made and the person who is present at the spot gets a copy, the witness or the person concerned, and then we keep a copy for the file.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: By whom was the INDA-BAU search record signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At INDA-BAU there were the signatures of Ms. Delalic and of Elvir Rizvanovic, and Navrat, Knauder and Klauser, those three being the police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Was there a time when Mr. Mucic was required to sign the search record of INDA-BAU?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, that wasn't the case, but he couldn't have signed it because it's a record, and only those present would sign that record, the Niederschrift, and as Mucic was not present at the search he should not sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Was there a time when Mucic was requested to sign the INDA-BAU search warrant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The search warrant that Mucic received, there were various addresses on there, and the person concerned of the search as ordered by the court was in each and every instance Mucic, so he was the person concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did he then put his signature on the search warrant for that reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He received it, but I can't say whether he signed the search warrant or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Going back to the material which was seized in the INDA-BAU premises and you said Mr. Navrat brought into Room 331 where was all this material contained? I mean again into bags or boxes. How many bags or boxes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a sports bag. In Taubergasse 15, Door 14, Mucic's things were put into boxes the things from INDA-BAU were taken. They were already in boxes so they were just kept in boxes or, shall we say, taken out, had a look and put back into boxes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Were there any folders or files of written documents among the material seized in the INDA-BAU premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were documents and files. As far as I can remember there were 12 folders.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there any video tapes among the INDA-BAU material?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a large number of videotapes were seized.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you remember -- as far as you can remember, how many videotapes were seized in the INDA-BAU premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 50 videotapes. There were a few problems and apparently there was a miscount, but roughly 50, 51. It said 51 and then it turned out to be 54.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: How many videotapes were seized in Mr. Delalic's apartment approximately, as far as you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So you have been saying about some mistake in the counting of the videotapes. What kind of a mistake in the counting of the videotapes took place and when was it corrected, if any time? Can you explain this point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of the file, Taubergasse 15, Door 10, I think in that instance it was corrected right away. That was noted into the record by the way. With regard to INDA-BAU, that was only corrected subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Again about the videotapes, were the videotapes classified with some sticker, some labels, some numbering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After they were seized the videotapes from Mucic's apartment were numbered on the same day, on 18th March, and with regard to the numbering of the other videos, they were numbered the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And some stickers were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stickers were put on the videotapes. The ones from Mucic's apartment were given an "M" for "Mucic" and then we put in numbers 1A, 1B, 1C, 1D, and the videotapes that were numbered later on, that is to say from INDA-BAU, and those from Taubergasse 15, Door 14, they were given numbers as following: "I" for "INDA-BAU".

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And then the additional number that would come after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What about the tapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the others for Delalic, they were given a "D" "and then a number after that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you personally do this operation of putting stickers with numbers on the videotapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not for the videotapes, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Who did that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Panzer did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, did you see in that same day of March 18th any investigator or anyway any officer of ICTY?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were people from the Tribunal who were --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the office, in Room 331.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you say how many were they and who were they, if possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were four persons there. One of them was an interpreter, a woman. With regard to the other people, I can't remember their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Approximately at what time did they arrive in Room 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when we'd started with the record, the Niederschrift, we began with that at 7.30 pm with Mucic, and at that time those persons were no longer present.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I didn't get you exactly. At what time did they arrive in Room 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between 5 o'clock and 7.30 then. They were present during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Was there any time when Mr. Mucic could remain alone with any ICTY officer that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not in the office throughout, but I wouldn't think so. Mucic was arrested by us and it's not customary and it's something you shouldn't do to leave him alone with those people, and the interpreter I said was there as well, so I would rule out that possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. What did the ICTY officers do after their arrival at Room 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, Gschwendt told me that these persons had the possibility of having a look at the seized documents and the videos, that this had been agreed with the judge, and the interpreter looked at the seized papers. So Gschwendt gave me the order to make copies of the seized material that were subsequently given to the people from the Tribunal. This was all with the agreement of Judge Seda. That's what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did the ICTY officers request to watch some videos too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and they were given that possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: When was that possibility given to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was during that time period, between 5.00 and 7.30 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: How many videos they could watch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The four videos from Mucic's apartment, but they weren't looked at in their entirety. They were just briefly viewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Were you with them in this watching operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Were all the ICTY people present involved in this watching?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: How many of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At times there was only one person and at other times there were two people involved in watching the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Was this videotape watching done in Room 331 or in a separate room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was in a separate room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: How did you proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we put the tapes in the VCR -- it's a bit complicated but anyway. We also tried to make a copy right away, because the court had authorised videotapes -- copies of videos to be handed over to people from the Tribunal, but that didn't work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So you say you didn't see entirely these tapes anyway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: How long did that take, this watching operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What about the request of ICTY people concerning copies of some documents, too? What did they exactly request to have immediately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had the documents to be copied. I had the folders and the documents were in there, and then I took those documents into a different room and made copies, but I made two copies of the documents, a copy of which was given to the Tribunal people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, my question was: did this request concern a selected number of documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the Tribunal interpreter flipped through the folders and wanted to have copies of certain documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Approximately how many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, about 30-50 pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Okay. Was it done again with the permission of Mr. Gschwendt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And with the permission of the judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It went via Department 210 again, it was Department 210 that discussed this with Judge Seda. That is how it happened but Gschwendt told me to make the copies and it was known there had been consultation with the court about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So you personally photocopied these selected documents; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: When did you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now was it before the videos or after the videos? I can't really say but in pretty much the same time-frame, between 5.00 and 7.30 in the afternoon. Yes, it is between 5.30 and 7.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you do that in Room 331 or in a separate room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the copy room is at the other end of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: How long did this photocopying operation take approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
