utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I ask your Honours to allow the witness to consult his own notes and material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. Go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the report -- this is contained in the report on 22nd April 1996 concerning Mr. Zdravko Mucic and the search in Austria 17 (sic), Taubergasse 15, Doors 10 and 14. In this report -- oh, excuse me. The report of 22nd April, Taubergasse 15, Door 10, under M6 of the classified items we classified this passport, M6.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you say briefly how is this document identified in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On page 2 of this report it is described. It was a Yugoslav passport with the number BH 978394, which was issued in the name of Zdravko Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the convenience of your Honours and the defence counsel, I will say that the English translation of the big report, so the English translation numbered as document 104A, has a continuous page numbering, and the page mentioned by the witness now corresponds to page 4 of the English translation. Now may I ask you, Mr. Moerbauer, to go back to the binder of the original items, and can you now look at the third document included in the binder, which is document 106, marked as 106 for the purposes of identification, the third document in the binder?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is once again a Yugoslav passport issued in the name of Zdravko Mucic, registration number BHR number 592332 and this passport was also classified as M6 amongst the seized items, and it is contained in the same report as the first item that I mentioned before. So this passport is listed -- is given, described in the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The same page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the same page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. May I now ask you to look at the third -- I mean at the fourth document included in the binder, which is the document marked for identification with number 107? Can you identify this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was also found in the apartment of Zdravko Mucic. It was found -- was classified under the number M6 and described as such in the report, and this is on page 2 of the report of 22nd April 1996, concerning the items seized from Taubergasse Number 15, Door 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So again on the same page of the report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the same page of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Is that described with some particular word?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was given under M6.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: But how is it defined in the report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's in the report -- it's stated: "Identity card in plastic wrap".

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the report it is stated: "Two identity cards in plastic wrap".

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now look at the fifth document included in the binder, which is marked for identification with number 108? Can you identify this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now in the report it says that this was secured in the apartment Taubergasse 15, Door 10, and that was in the M6 folder. That went to the court, and this is one of the two identification cards in plastic wrap.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I will ask the Registry to provide the witness with the four videotapes, which were numbered for identification as 109, 110, 111 and 112. I will tell the witness that he can skip what appears in the binder concerning these videos, because they are simply the English transcripts of the videos. That's not useful for identification purposes. You can see that these are four videotapes and, Mr. Moerbauer, I ask you whether you can recognise for the moment these four videotapes for their external appearance and for the labels which appear on them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This videotape, or I should say the cover, has the number "M1A", and on that basis stems from Zdravko Mucic's apartment, according to the label on the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes. Can you look at the other ones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There's a sticker on here and on the cassette there's the number "M1A", so that is on the cassette itself, that reference. So this is from Zdravko Mucic's apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the second videotape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here again "M1B", both the tape and the case, and therefore stem from the apartment of Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. You see then the third tape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This tape is referred the same way, both the tape and the cover, "M1C", and also stems from Zdravko Mucic's apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. The fourth one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This videotape is lettered "M1D" and that's the same address, Taubergasse 15, 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So again the apartment of Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the apartment of Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now can you find the mention of these four videotapes in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These videotapes are mentioned in the report of 22nd April 1996 regarding Zdravko Mucic and the search of 1170 Vienna, Taubergasse 15/Door 10. This is on the first page there regarding the analysis and here's mentioned the individual tapes with a description of the contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Again for the convenience of your Honours and the defence lawyers, may I say that this page corresponds to page 5 and page 6 of the English translation of the final report. Now, Mr. Moerbauer, could you further recognise and identify these tapes if you should see them played in part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of the contents I could recognise the videos. I know pretty much what's in those or on those tapes, but were I to see all of them, I couldn't say whether it came from INDA-BAU or from Mucic. With the report I could compare and that way I could ascertain that it was the videotape that was seized and is mentioned in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So may I invite the technicians to play the excerpt video concerning the first videotape?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Judge, I object to playing something that's not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: For identification purposes again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Has he not identified it by its numbering or whatever mark he made on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: If your Honours and the defence lawyers deem that this identification is sufficient, and there is a kind of a stipulation on that, we do not object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: When they were numbered individually, they did not play it, did they?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: At the time the videos were collected from the accused persons, they were not played. They must have been played in their station.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, they were played during his examination in the police headquarters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, but that is after you had removed them from the premises from where they took them. So the identifying mark which you made at the time you took it is the relevant thing, not whether you played it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. Then we accept that the videotapes were identified the way we are doing and we proceed to the next items, your Honours. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so the record is clear, we are not waiving any kind of objections. I thought we were going to take objections at the end of all these when he offered them into evidence. MR. OLUJIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, if I may be allowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes? MR. OLUJIC (in interpretation): We should like to object along those lines. What I said at the beginning, the witness could simply state his views regarding authenticity. All objections will come later. So let there be no confusion. Yes, the object was identified and nothing more, not the contents, nor anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So this is the situation, your Honours. We believe that we should allow the witness to see at least a small part of the tapes until he might say something about his being in a position to identify also the interior, the internal part of the tape and not only the external appearance. So again I would ask the technicians to play at least a part of the tapes, a few minutes of the tape, until the witness can say "yes" or "no" on his possibility of identifying these items not only for the paper external appearance but only for their content following to the thoroughly examination he did between March and April 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, he has already testified that he could look at the tapes and say: "I know these were some of the tapes but I couldn't tell you without looking at the paper stickers where they came from". He's testifying that this was seized from a location based upon the paper stickers on the outside of the objects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There's just one small point. You said there was miscounting of the videotapes. Actually there were 54 and not 51.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, these four videotapes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I'm just talking about another point altogether. Look at your annexure 1A. At the end there is a report by Panzer and this witness. Page 3 of this report talks of 83 video cassettes seized, 54 from INDA-BAU, 28 from Delalic's flat and 4 from Mucic's. The number comes to 86. You said 83. So there's a discrepancy of three. There was again a miscounting or what? If the number is 51, then, of course, it will add up to 83, but here -- this is 1A, page 3 of the translation. Have you got it? Have you got these figures?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, we've found this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You get 83.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, you will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Actually if you count 54, plus 28, plus 4, it comes to 86. There is a discrepancy of three again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You will see the same mistake is in the original. Can you explain something about that, Mr. Moerbauer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The report is signed by this witness along with Panzer. Are you sure it was 54?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a counting mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Here again if you add 54, plus 28, plus 4, it comes to 86, but you see the figure 83 which was seized. Are you sure it was 51, not 54?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On page 1 it says 86 videotapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I'm just looking at the translation of the report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the same report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I'm just looking at the English translation of your report. It's at 1A. Maybe it's a typing mistake, because I don't understand German. I can't read German. Have you noticed this discrepancy?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. The witness says that on another page he says the right number, 86. On which page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let's not behave like children here, if there has been an analysing error. You are proceeding with getting him to identify the cassettes. Let's go on and deal with that. He has seen those cassettes. It is not plain that he identified them. If they had any marks on them, let him tell us what marks he made on them which enabled him to identify them when he took them from those places where he seized them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, on these four videotapes there are marks. What marks did you make on these video cassettes which enable you to identify them as the ones you took from the apartment of Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, with regard to these four tapes that were secured in Mucic's apartment, these were the first videos that were numbered the same day. The other tapes were not numbered, and these were the first video tapes that were copied. The copies were handed over to the Tribunal. So these are the four videotapes that I've seen the most of, because I saw the whole of them while they were being played, and it would not have been possible to mix these up, because the other tapes were given a consecutive number later on. They just got a number and they didn't get the additional letter. We decided on that later, that we wouldn't put any letters on the tapes, but here we do have a letter, because these are the first ones we looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So did you recognise the stickers and markings on the four videotapes you just looked at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are the references put on them by Panzer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Is Panzer coming to give evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honours, if the court deems that useful, certainly we will have other police officers from the Vienna police to come and testify in the future of this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Because it was him who secured these tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I see what you mean. So we'll be -- we will certainly be in a position to call Mr. Panzer, Mr. Navrat and possibly other police officers. Mr. Moerbauer, did you see the stickers put on these four videotapes by Mr. Panzer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. May I ask you, Mr. Moerbauer, to look at the document following the transcript of the four videotapes in the binder of the original, that is to say document number 10 in the binder, which is marked for identification as document 113? Can you find this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 117?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: According to the marking done of the Registrar today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to disturb the peace of my learned friend's examination-in-chief. I think there is a witness in the public gallery, who is a potential witness for the Prosecution on this issue of continuity, who should not be there, Sabine Manke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Is one of your witnesses still sitting?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Probably we didn't plan to call her again, but anyway --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The Prosecution has been mentioning a number of other people they might want to be calling on this issue of continuity. As a matter of safety first she should not be in the public gallery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: In the interests of caution she had better not be.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I think it is good for her to be invited to leave the courtroom, court gallery. She left immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now document 113, according to the index, D4/3 is the reference we put on that, D4/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you identify that and say where was it seized?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now this document was among the items seized at Taubergasse 15, Door 10, and it was in the folder that's D4, and that was on the third page there. It was the third document to be examined.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: But in which premises was that seized? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): An objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not secured by me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Hold on. Let's hear the objection. Yes, let's hear it. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): The witness has testified that he did not seize objects in the Taubergasse apartment. He's not a person that can identify the confiscated objects and therefore this object too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I respond, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Well, let's hear you. Let's hear your response.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In our submission this particular document can be identified also by this witness, because anyway this is the witness who made the thoroughly examination of all the seized documents. Of course, as I already said, the Prosecution is accepting the idea of calling as witnesses also the police officers, the Vienna police who carried on the different investigations, the different house searches, but in any case nothing denies the possibility that a document might be identified by more than one witness according to what each one of them has done in his official capacity concerning a given document. This witness concerning this document did an examination with the interpreter, as he did that examination on the other documents. So, in our submission, these documents which he examined thoroughly might be identified both through him and through any other person, including the officer who took part in the house search in the apartment of Mr. Delalic. On the other hand, we would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: We have had that twice now. I think it is all right. You've repeated the same thing twice. You have said since he did some work on the documents, he can identify it. Now, as long as there is a person who actually seized the document and he is coming to give evidence, it is unnecessary multiplying the number of people who identify these documents. So I do not think it is necessary to put any document to him to identify something which another witness is coming to identify. So it's not necessary. I agree with the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He examined the documents all right, but seized where? It's only the person who seized them can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I see the point, your Honours, but the person who received the documents seized --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I've made the ruling, so find something else to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, your Honour. We would ask the Registrar to provide the witness with the four -- with the three videotapes, unless, being 5.30 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, it is 5.30. Perhaps it might be better for you go home, look at your case properly and know how to introduce the evidence. One has been a little patient listening to a lot of confusion here and I don't enjoy it at all. So please kindly look at your case properly and bring those who you know actually seized these documents so that they'll identify them properly in accordance with the procedure of identifying documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, first of all, if any member of the prosecution staff was offended by my remarks prior to the last break, I want to extend my apologies. I hold all of them in very, very high regard. I consider them colleagues of the highest professional standing, and if the court was offended in any way by those remarks, I want to apologise also. Secondly, I would like to ask the Prosecution to give us the list of witnesses they would expect to be calling next week, so that we can have the weekend to prepare. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ackerman. I think that is the real professional way of dealing with little disagreements of this nature, and I'm sure Ms. McHenry accepts the apology.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Of course, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will now rise. (5.30 pm)
